coverage_gaps: Mexico (JUR-0077): regulator is SEGOB's Dirección General de Juegos y Sorteos under the Federal Law on Games and Lotteries (1947); online sites must be tied to a land-based permit holder; IEPS on online gambling raised to 50% from 1 Jan 2026; SEGOB finished a draft replacement law in Sept-Oct 2026 and suspended 10 online casino domains in July 2026 (trade press). No SEGOB/DOF URL seen.

Croatia (JUR-0082): Ministry of Finance (games of chance department) licenses; online casino requires a land-based casino concession; 2025 amendment (NN 72/2025) and 2026 fee and tax rises (trade press). No Ministry of Finance or Narodne novine URL seen.

Angola (JUR-0029): Gaming Activity Law 17/24 of 28 Oct 2024 replaced Law 5/16; regulator ISJ (Instituto de Supervisão de Jogos) issues online licences, with a 30-day transitional window and active blocking of unlicensed sites in 2026. Only lex.ao (private portal) surfaced; no ISJ or Diário da República URL.

Kosovo (JUR-0050): Law on the Prohibition of Games of Chance in force since 2019 for 10 years (all gambling banned except the Kosovo lottery). Label 'Prohibited' looks correct. A draft law URL exists on kryeministri.rks-gov.net but is a draft; not listed.

Cote D'Ivoire (JUR-0066): regulator ARJH (since 2021) under Law 2020-480; Dec 2023 decrees reserve sports and horse betting (physical and online) to LONACI; other online games need ARJH authorisation. No ARJH URL seen.
Tanzania (JUR-0094): regulator is the Gaming Board of Tanzania under the Gaming Act Cap. 41; online casino and sports betting licensed (about 30 operators, trade sources). No GBT URL seen.
Serbia: online licences for special games exist; classical games (lottery, bingo) online are state lottery only (Legal500).
Estonia: B2C only licensed; no B2B licence; software suppliers need no licence; EEA licences not recognised (Legal500).
Still unchecked from the unclear group: Papua New Guinea, Zimbabwe, Bolivia, Cameroon, Virgin Islands (UK), Paraguay, El Salvador, Myanmar, Namibia.
Labels that look wrong: Tanzania (licensed online market, regulator active), Angola (licensing open under 2024 law), Cote D'Ivoire (regulated, partly LONACI monopoly). Kosovo looks correct.
